summary: The root هزم (hzm) primarily refers to a depression, dint, or small hollow. It can describe the pit between collarbones, a pit above a horse's eye, or even the purring sound from a cat's throat.
lane: هَزْمَةٌ ذ The [ purring, or] sound of the throat of a cat. (TA.) -b2- The pit between the two collar-bones. (TA, art. ترب .) -b3- [The pit above a horse's eye.] (K, voce وَقْبٌ .) See also خُنْعُبَةٌ , and قَلْتَةٌ : and see عُقْمٌ , where it seems to mean a stricture: it generally and properly signifies a depression, or dint: or a pit, or small hollow, resembling a dint: see also غَيْبٌ .

headwords.def: اِنْهَزَمَ It (an army) was routed, discomfited, defeated, or put to flight. (K, &c.) See حَاصَ, in art. حيص; and اِنْحَازَ, in art. حوز; from both of which it is distinguished.

هَزْمَةٌ The [ purring, or] sound of the throat of a cat. (TA.) The pit between the two collar-bones. (TA, art. ترب.) [The pit above a horse's eye.] (K, voce وَقْبٌ.) See also خُنْعُبَةٌ, and قَلْتَةٌ: and see عُقْمٌ, where it seems to mean a stricture: it generally and properly signifies a depression, or dint: or a pit, or small hollow, resembling a dint: see also غَيْبٌ.
مَهْزُومُ الصَّدْرِ Depressed of breast, i. e., apparently, illiberal, niggardly: see حَوْضٌ.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
